formats.key: setup(address[] _owners, uint256 _threshold, address to, bytes data, address fallbackHandler, address paymentToken, uint256 payment, address paymentReceiver)
effects: Sets the Safe owner list to _owners and the confirmation threshold to _threshold, once only.
Sets fallbackHandler as the fallback handler when it is not the zero address.
Runs `data` as a DELEGATECALL to `to` in the Safe's own context, so `to`'s code can change any Safe storage or move any Safe asset.
When payment > 0, the Safe pays `payment` of paymentToken (ETH when zero) to paymentReceiver, or to tx.origin when paymentReceiver is zero.
On the bound singleton addresses the call always reverts (the constructor sets threshold = 1, so GS200).
formats.shown: "Setup Safe" with the owner list, a raw threshold, the fallback handler, the payment in its token, the payment receiver, and `data` decoded as a normal call to `to` under the label "Module".

findings.title: setup decodes `data` as a normal call to `to`, but the Safe runs it as a delegate call.
findings.evidence: ModuleManager.setupModules: `require(execute(to, 0, data, Enum.Operation.DelegateCall, gasleft()), "GS000");`. Descriptor setup field `data`: label "Module", format "calldata", params {"calleePath": "to"}.
findings.fix: Change the label to "Delegate call (runs in the Safe)". Add a field for `to` labelled "Delegate call target". Do not decode `data` as a call to `to`; show it raw, or state in the intent that setup runs code as the Safe.

findings.title: setup labels the delegate call payload "Module", but no module is enabled.
findings.evidence: ModuleManager.setupModules only sets `modules[SENTINEL_MODULES] = SENTINEL_MODULES` and delegate-calls `to`; no enableModule. Descriptor: "label": "Module".
findings.fix: Change the label to "Initializer call" and add a field for `to`.

findings.title: setup shows a zero payment receiver literally, but the code then pays tx.origin.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.handlePayment: `address payable receiver = refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver;`. Descriptor field paymentReceiver has no senderAddress.
findings.fix: Add "senderAddress": "$.metadata.constants.addressAsNull" to the paymentReceiver params, or a label "Payment receiver (zero = transaction sender)".

findings.title: setup is bound to the Safe singletons, where setup always reverts; real Safes are proxies.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe constructor: `threshold = 1;` with the comment "it is not possible to call setup anymore". OwnerManager.setupOwners: `require(threshold == 0, "GS200");`. Deployments list only 0xd9db270c… and 0x69f4d178….
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies, for example with a factory constraint on the GnosisSafeProxyFactory ProxyCreation event, instead of the singleton addresses.

findings.title: setup intent "Setup Safe" does not say that it sets owners, runs a delegate call and may pay.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "intent": "Setup Safe", no interpolatedIntent. GnosisSafe.setup calls setupOwners, setupModules (delegate call) and handlePayment.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Create Safe with {_threshold} of owners, pay {payment}".

formats.key: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
effects: The signer's msg.value (native currency) goes to the Safe; the function is payable.
The Safe calls `to` with `value` native currency from the Safe's balance and `data`, or delegate-calls `to` when operation = 1, running `to`'s code in the Safe's context.
Increments the Safe nonce and consumes the signatures of the owners.
When gasPrice > 0, the Safe pays (gasUsed + baseGas) * gasPrice in gasToken (ETH when zero) to refundReceiver, or to tx.origin when it is zero, even if the inner call fails.
When safeTxGas or gasPrice is non-zero, a failing inner call does not revert; the nonce and the refund are still spent.
A guard configured in storage may check the call before and after execution.
formats.shown: "sign multisig operation" with the operation type, the Safe, the executing signer, the inner call decoded against `to`, raw baseGas, the gas price in gasToken and the gas receiver; safeTxGas and signatures hidden; no field for msg.value, `to` or `value`.

findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows the native value the signer sends.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.execTransaction: `) public payable virtual returns (bool success)`. Descriptor execTransaction fields have no "@.value" path.
findings.fix: Add {"path": "@.value", "label": "ETH sent to Safe", "format": "amount", "visible": {"ifNotIn": ["0"]}}.

findings.title: execTransaction shows no field for the recipient `to` or the native `value` the Safe sends.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.execTransaction: `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, ...)`; Executor: `call(txGas, to, value, ...)`. Descriptor: `to` is used only as calleePath and `value` only as amountPath of the field "Transaction". For a plain ETH transfer `data` is empty and nothing shows the amount or the recipient.
findings.fix: Add {"path": "to", "label": "To", "format": "addressName"} and {"path": "value", "label": "Amount", "format": "amount"}, and add an interpolatedIntent such as "Safe sends {value} to {to}".

findings.title: execTransaction decodes `data` as a call to `to`, but operation 1 runs it as a delegate call.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, ...) }`. Descriptor field "Transaction": format calldata, calleePath "to", spenderPath "@.to".
findings.fix: Do not decode `data` as a call to `to` when operation is 1. Split into two formats or show a fixed warning "Runs code of {to} inside the Safe" when operation is 1.

findings.title: execTransaction hides safeTxGas, which decides if a failing inner call still pays the refund.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.execTransaction: `require(success || safeTxGas != 0 || gasPrice != 0, "GS013");` and the refund uses gasUsed bounded by safeTxGas. Descriptor: {"path": "safeTxGas", "visible": "never"}.
findings.fix: Show safeTxGas with visible ifNotIn ["0"], label "Gas limit of inner call".

findings.title: execTransaction shows gas price and base gas separately, not the total refund the Safe pays.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.handlePayment: `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice)`. Descriptor fields "Gas amount" (raw baseGas) and "Gas price" (tokenAmount).
findings.fix: Change the labels to "Refund base gas" and "Refund price per gas", and hide both with ifNotIn ["0"] on gasPrice.

findings.title: execTransaction shows a zero refund receiver literally, but the code pays tx.origin.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.handlePayment: `refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver`. Descriptor field "Gas receiver" has no senderAddress.
findings.fix: Add "senderAddress": "$.metadata.constants.addressAsNull" to the refundReceiver params.

findings.title: execTransaction intent "sign multisig operation" says nothing about what the Safe does.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "intent": "sign multisig operation", interpolatedIntent null. The function executes a call or delegate call from the Safe with its assets.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Execute Safe transaction" and add an interpolatedIntent naming {to} and {value}.

findings.title: execTransaction is bound to the Safe singletons, where it always reverts; real Safes are proxies.
findings.evidence: On the singleton ownerCount is 0, so GnosisSafe.checkNSignatures always fails `owners[currentOwner] != address(0)` (GS026). Deployments list only the singleton addresses.
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies with a factory constraint on the proxy factory.

effects: Adds `owner` as a Safe owner.
Sets the threshold to _threshold when it differs from the current one.
Only the Safe itself may call it (authorized); a direct call reverts, as in case 0.
formats.shown: "Add signer" with the new signer address and the new threshold.

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold is bound to the singleton and called directly, so it always reverts.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.addOwnerWithThreshold is `public authorized`; SelfAuthorized requires msg.sender == address(this). Case 0: mined status 0, effects [], sent to 0xd9db270c… (singleton). The reader believed an owner was added.
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies, and render this format as the nested call of execTransaction with `to` = the Safe.

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold intent "Add signer" omits the threshold change it can make.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.addOwnerWithThreshold: `if (threshold != _threshold) changeThreshold(_threshold);`. Descriptor: "intent": "Add signer", interpolatedIntent null.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent "Add signer {owner}, threshold {_threshold}".

cases.notes: The mined tx reverted (status 0, no effects): a direct call to the singleton fails the authorized check. The reader believed an owner was added and the threshold set to 1.

Sets the threshold to _threshold when it differs from the current one.
Only the Safe itself may call it; a direct call reverts, as in case 1.
formats.shown: "Remove signer" with the removed signer and the new threshold; prevOwner hidden.

findings.title: removeOwner is bound to the singleton and called directly, so it always reverts.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.removeOwner is `public authorized`. Case 1: mined status 0, effects [], sent to the singleton 0xd9db270c…. The reader believed the signer lost owner rights.
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies, and render this format as the nested call of execTransaction.

findings.title: removeOwner intent "Remove signer" omits the threshold change it can make.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.removeOwner: `if (threshold != _threshold) changeThreshold(_threshold);`. Descriptor: "intent": "Remove signer".
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent "Remove signer {owner}, threshold {_threshold}".

cases.notes: The mined tx reverted (status 0, no effects). The reader believed the owner was removed and the threshold set to 1.

formats.key: swapOwner(address prevOwner, address oldOwner, address newOwner)
effects: Replaces oldOwner with newOwner in the Safe owner list; the threshold does not change.
Only the Safe itself may call it; a direct call reverts, as in case 2.
formats.shown: "Swap signer" with the old signer and the new signer; prevOwner hidden.

findings.title: swapOwner is bound to the singleton and called directly, so it always reverts.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.swapOwner is `public authorized`. Case 2: mined status 0, effects [], sent to the singleton 0xd9db270c…. The reader believed their address became a signer.
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies, and render this format as the nested call of execTransaction.

Only the Safe itself may call it; a direct call to the singleton reverts.

findings.title: changeThreshold is bound to the singleton, where a direct call always reverts.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.changeThreshold is `public authorized`; the deployments are the singleton addresses only.
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies.

effects: Records hashToApprove as approved by the signer; it then counts as the signer's signature (v = 1) for the Safe transaction with that hash.
The caller must be a Safe owner, so it reverts on the singleton.
formats.shown: "Approve Safe hash" with the raw 32-byte hash.

findings.title: approveHash shows only a hash; it stands for a Safe transaction the screen cannot decode.
findings.evidence: GnosisSafe.checkNSignatures: `require(msg.sender == currentOwner || approvedHashes[currentOwner][dataHash] != 0, "GS025");`. GnosisSafe.approveHash: `approvedHashes[msg.sender][hashToApprove] = 1;`. Descriptor field hashToApprove format raw.

findings.title: approveHash intent does not say that the approval acts as the signer's signature.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "intent": "Approve Safe hash". The approved hash replaces an owner signature in checkNSignatures.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Sign Safe transaction by hash".

findings.format: setup(address[] _owners, uint256 _threshold, address to, bytes data, address fallbackHandler, address paymentToken, uint256 payment, address paymentReceiver)
findings.title: setup decodes `data` as a normal call to `to`, but the Safe runs it as a delegate call.
findings.reason: setup always runs `data` as a delegate call, so `to`'s code runs in the Safe's own context and storage. The descriptor decodes `data` as a plain call to `to`, labels it "Module", and no field or intent says it is a delegate call. The severity guide's examples name this exact pattern as critical.
findings.quote: ModuleManager.setupModules: `if (to != address(0)) require(execute(to, 0, data, Enum.Operation.DelegateCall, gasleft()), "GS000");` — descriptor setup field: {"path": "data", "label": "Module", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "to"}}

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows the native value the signer sends.
findings.reason: execTransaction is payable and no check forces msg.value to zero. The Safe keeps any ETH the signer sends, and `execute` can forward it. No field shows `@.value`, so ETH leaves the signer's wallet in an amount the screen never shows.
findings.quote: GnosisSafe.execTransaction: `) public payable virtual returns (bool success) {` — no require on msg.value anywhere in the body; descriptor execTransaction fields: operation, @.to, @.from, data, baseGas, gasPrice, refundReceiver, safeTxGas, signatures (no @.value)

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction shows no field for the recipient `to` or the native `value` the Safe sends.
findings.reason: `to` and `value` are only passed as parameters to the nested call. They are not fields of their own, and the spec only lets the nested descriptor show the amount ("MAY"). For a plain ETH transfer with empty `data` there is no nested descriptor, so nothing shows the amount. The spec fallback only "MAY" show the target, so the recipient is not guaranteed either.
findings.quote: Executor.execute: `success := call(txGas, to, value, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0)`; descriptor field "Transaction" {format: calldata, calleePath: "to", amountPath: "value"}; spec erc-7730.md: amountPath "If provided, the ERC-7730 descriptor for this embedded calldata MAY reference this value using the @.value container path"

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction decodes `data` as a call to `to`, but operation 1 runs it as a delegate call.
findings.reason: With operation 1 the Safe runs `to`'s code in its own context. The nested rendering still describes a normal call to `to`, such as a token transfer, which does not happen as shown. The "Operation type: Delegate Call" enum is shown, but it does not correct the nested call's stated outcome. The severity guide lists this exact pattern as critical.
findings.quote: Executor.execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0) }`; descriptor field "Transaction": {"format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "to", "amountPath": "value", "spenderPath": "@.to"}}

findings.format: setup(address[] _owners, uint256 _threshold, address to, bytes data, address fallbackHandler, address paymentToken, uint256 payment, address paymentReceiver)
findings.title: setup decodes `data` as a normal call to `to`, but the Safe runs it as a delegate call.
findings.reason: Setup executes the supplied code in the Safe’s storage and balance context. Neither “Setup Safe” nor the “Module” field states that this is a delegate call.
findings.quote: contracts/1-0xd9db270c1b5e3bd161e8c8503c55ceabee709552/src/contracts/base/ModuleManager.sol, setupModules: `require(execute(to, 0, data, Enum.Operation.DelegateCall, gasleft()), "GS000");`. descriptor.json, setup: `"intent": "Setup Safe"`; data field: `"label": "Module", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "to"}`.

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows the native value the signer sends.
findings.reason: A valid execution with no guard, zero outgoing value, and zero gasPrice retains ETH attached by the signer. No field displays that incoming value; the nested amountPath references the separate outgoing value parameter.
findings.quote: contracts/1-0xd9db270c1b5e3bd161e8c8503c55ceabee709552/src/contracts/GnosisSafe.sol, execTransaction: `) public payable virtual returns (bool success)`; `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, gasPrice == 0 ? (gasleft() - 2500) : safeTxGas);`; `if (gasPrice > 0) { payment = handlePayment(gasUsed, baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken, refundReceiver); }`. The function contains no msg.value check or refund. descriptor.json, execTransaction: `"label": "Transaction", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "to", "amountPath": "value", "spenderPath": "@.to"}`; its complete fields list contains no `@.value`.

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction shows no field for the recipient `to` or the native `value` the Safe sends.
findings.reason: The visible Transaction field supplies both recipient and native amount through calldata formatting parameters. The claim that empty calldata hides both depends on unprovided rendering behavior, which the guide excludes from critical findings.
findings.quote: descriptor.json, execTransaction Transaction field: `"params": {"calleePath": "to", "amountPath": "value", "spenderPath": "@.to"}, "visible": "always"`. Registry specs/erc7730-v2.schema.json, calldataParameters.amountPath: `"description": "The path to the associated amount in native currency, if the calldata can be associated with a container value."`. Registry .github/scripts/ai-review/prompt.md, not_critical item 14: `a nested descriptor that might not resolve, a lookup that may fail`.

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
